rv.q: There’s no doubting the talent and sincerity involved in Already Perfect, and Kreis himself brings a big voice to this small stage.
You'll rarely witness a better musical production at an intimate fringe venue, than this.
Thankfully not – because the past, reimagined here, has produced a superb piece of musical theatre that absolutely deserves to be seen.

More often than not, though, the narrative feels stiffly chronological, and the occasional fourth wall break or unreliable narrator is a welcome relief from a rehashed queer coming-of-age story we’ve all seen before.
Ultimately, one can’t help wishing they’d just ditch the script and give us a terrific Levi Kreis concert.
Underlying the drama is a deep hankering for the bad old days when gay sex was taboo and when every fling was risky, rebellious and exhilarating.
Already Perfect is hugely entertaining, with powerful songs that complement without swamping the action.
The songs are what lifts Already Perfect.

cn.t: Critics are mixed on Kreis' semi-autobiographical musical, praising its soulful score and raw personal storytelling while questioning whether the deeply personal narrative achieves universal resonance beyond its creator's own journey.
